title: The Burning Salt
premise: Juniper Whitlock has spent his life guarding the Saltgate, a sealed mountain pass that once let the old gods walk the world — and keeping the fact of his own divine blood a secret even from the smugglers who trust him. When prayers begin to be answered again and pilgrims flood Thornfell, Juniper discovers his late mother's covenant is unraveling: the gate opens only for one of her line, and both the resurrected god Veyra and the war-hungry Order of the Iron Bell want him. Torn between love for a pilgrim healer named Sable, who carries her own forbidden faith, and duty to the valley that would burn him as an abomination if they knew what he is, Juniper must choose whether to reseal the gate forever or open it. In the end he splits himself between worlds — mortal keeper below, dying god above — buying peace at the cost of ever being whole again.
about_author: Jude Almeida is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent six years mapping remote mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about borders, both geographic and spiritual, from a farmhouse full of unreliable clocks.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Ledger
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He walks his smuggling routes through Thornfell, cataloguing travelers and hiding his strange affinity for the old shrine stones. Establishes his loneliness, his dead mother's cryptic warnings, and the routine he mistakes for safety. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath competence.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A dying shepherd's desperate prayer at a ruined altar is inexplicably granted; the man's flock returns overnight. Juniper finds the altar warm and carved with his mother's sigil. Emotional beat: first crack in the world's logic, and in his denial.

chapters.title: The Pilgrim Road
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A healer-pilgrim arrives leading a ragged column of believers toward Thornfell, fleeing persecution by the Order of the Iron Bell. She notices the gatekeeper watching them with recognition rather than contempt. Emotional beat: wary hope on the road.

chapters.title: Iron Bells in the Pass
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Order inquisitors arrive demanding passage and the surrender of 'god-touched' pilgrims. Juniper lies smoothly but realizes the Order knows more about the Saltgate's bloodline than he does. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing he is also prey.

chapters.title: What Mother Buried
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Searching his mother's hidden cache beneath the gatehouse, he finds her covenant: she bound the gods out by binding her own divinity into the seal — a binding that dies with her bloodline. Emotional beat: grief curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: Salt and Smoke
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable treats wounded smugglers after an Order raid and glimpses Juniper healing a boy with a touch no human should have. She says nothing, but begins to understand why the road feels holy here. Emotional beat: tenderness entangled with dangerous knowledge.

chapters.title: Veyra Wakes
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. In a dream, the goddess Veyra speaks to him through the seal, offering restoration of the old world — and showing him the famine and war that followed her imprisonment. He wakes with frost on his lashes in midsummer. Emotional beat: seduction of a beautiful lie.

chapters.title: The Valley's Verdict
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The valley council debates the pilgrims' presence; fear wins, and harboring them becomes a crime. Juniper votes with the majority to protect his secret, then shelters Sable anyway. Emotional beat: cowardice and conscience in the same breath.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Faith
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable confronts Juniper about what she saw; he confesses his bloodline. Instead of recoiling, she tells him the pilgrims came because of dreams of a gatekeeper with his face. Emotional beat: intimacy forged from shared secrets.

chapters.title: The Order's Bargain
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Inquisitor-Captain Hale offers Juniper clemency for the valley if he surrenders himself and lets the Order destroy the gate permanently. Juniper stalls, learning the Order's true aim: not eradicating gods, but capturing one. Emotional beat: the trap closing gently.

chapters.title: Frost on the Shrine Stones
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Miracles multiply across Thornfell — some merciful, some monstrous — as Veyra's influence leaks through the weakening seal. Villagers turn on each other; a child is accused of witchcraft. Emotional beat: wonder rotting into mob fear.

chapters.title: Blood Is a Key
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Testing his mother's notes, Juniper discovers the gate responds to his blood — opening a hairline crack. Through it he hears ten thousand voices, worshipful and starving. Emotional beat: terror of his own power.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Choice
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. His oldest friend, smuggler Bram, offers to move Sable and the pilgrims over the western passes to safety — but only if Juniper abandons the gate. Duty and love pull in opposite directions for the first time openly. Emotional beat: heartbreak disguised as logistics.

chapters.title: Hale's Sermon
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. The inquisitor publicly burns a captured pilgrim in the valley square, preaching that mercy invited the gods back. He names the gatekeeper as a collaborator. Emotional beat: righteous cruelty, and the crowd's complicity.

chapters.title: Riot at the Gate
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The valley mobs the gatehouse; Sable is taken while shielding pilgrims. Juniper, to save her, bleeds on the seal deliberately — and the gate groans open a hand's width. Light spills through. Emotional beat: sacrifice triggering catastrophe.

chapters.title: What Came Through
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Not Veyra but her herald steps through — vast, patient, hungry for a vessel. It offers to trade Sable's life for Juniper's body. Juniper refuses and fights with stolen divine fire, wounding it but revealing himself to every witness. Emotional beat: the mask burned away forever.

chapters.title: Abomination
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The valley turns on Juniper; even grateful villagers call for his death. Sable breaks him out of the Order's holding cell, choosing exile over safety. Emotional beat: love against duty, made literal.

chapters.title: The Long Ascent
chapters.summary: Juniper and Sable's alternating POV. Fleeing up the forbidden face of the mountain toward the gate's heart, hunted by both Order and herald, they speak honestly about what each would sacrifice. Emotional beat: a love confession timed like a prayer.

chapters.title: Covenant Remade
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At the seal's heart, Juniper meets his mother's lingering echo, who begs forgiveness and shows him a third path: not sealing or opening, but becoming the gate himself. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed as choice, not sentence.

chapters.title: The Burning Salt
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Climax. Hale forces the gate wide with captured pilgrim blood; the herald pours through. Juniper accepts the covenant — burning his mortality as salt burns in a wound — and slams the gate shut from inside, casting Veyra's fragment and half of himself into the dark. Emotional beat: triumph priced in selfhood.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Miracle
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The Order fractures without its prize; the valley, ashamed, builds a shrine instead of a pyre. Sable tends the gatehouse where Juniper now exists half-present — warm hands, distant eyes. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude sharing a bed.

chapters.title: The Gatekeeper's Prayer
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, final chapter. From within the threshold, Juniper can hear prayers and answer small ones — rain, safe roads, healed children. Sable visits daily; sometimes he is fully there. He keeps the gate, and the gate keeps what remains of him. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace, love persisting across a threshold.
